frozen_at: 2026-11-13, before any retrieval run (only `prepare` had been executed)
author: Benchmark drafted with AI assistance (Claude) from data/pages.jsonl; every evidence_quote is machine-checked against the normalized gold page by `python -m src.run evaluate` before retrieval.
split_rule: Split by section to limit leakage: test questions come only from sections 3.6, 4.8, 4.10 and 5.5; no dev question has its gold evidence in those sections. 19 dev / 6 test.
filter_rule: `filter` is the scope the user supplies before retrieval (e.g. they are studying a given chapter). It is never derived from the gold answer. Strategy C applies it only when present; A and B ignore it. Filter questions are deliberately ambiguous across chapters without that scope.
selection_criterion: Pre-registered before viewing any results: choose the strategy with the highest dev Evidence Hit@3; ties broken by dev Hit@1, then by fewer stored chunks. Test is run once after the choice is fixed and reported as-is.

types.direct: answer stated plainly in one place
types.paraphrase: question wording differs from the source wording
types.conditional: answer depends on a condition or exception
types.metadata_filter: ambiguous across chapters; requires the user-supplied chapter scope

questions.question: Do I have to register my work with the government to get a copyright in the United States?
questions.expected_answer: No. Copyright is granted automatically at the moment of creation once the work is fixed in tangible form; registration is only required to bring an infringement suit in federal court.
questions.evidence_quote: Interestingly, registration is not required to obtain a copyright.

alternative_evidence.evidence_quote: registration is not required in order to enjoy copyright protection

questions.question: How long was the copyright term under England's Statute of Anne?
questions.expected_answer: 14 years, with the right to renew for one additional 14-year term (instead of a perpetual right).
questions.evidence_quote: the term was limited to 14 years with the right to renew for one additional 14-year term

questions.question: For how many years did America's first federal copyright law of 1790 protect a map, chart or book?
questions.expected_answer: 14 years, with the right of renewal for another 14 years (28 years maximum).
questions.evidence_quote: for a period of 14 years, with the right of renewal for another 14 years

questions.question: When does the copyright expire for a work made for hire or an anonymous work?
questions.expected_answer: 95 years from first publication or 120 years from the year of creation, whichever comes first.
questions.evidence_quote: the copyright term lasts 95 years from the first publication or 120 years from the year of the work’s creation, whichever comes first

alternative_evidence.evidence_quote: will last for 95 years from the year of first publication, or for 120 years from the year of its creation, whichever expires first

questions.question: Once a bookstore has bought copies of a novel, may it print additional copies of the book?
questions.expected_answer: No. The first-sale doctrine ends the author's distribution rights in those copies (the store may sell, rent or give them away) but does not limit the reproduction right.
questions.evidence_quote: The bookstore owner cannot, however, make additional copies of the book because the first-sale doctrine does not limit a copyright owner’s reproduction right

questions.question: Why is Einstein's famous mass-energy equation not protected by copyright?
questions.expected_answer: It is an abstract idea derived from observing natural physical laws, so it must stay in the public domain so research and teaching are not blocked.
questions.evidence_quote: the formula was derived from observation of natural physical laws, and must remain in the public domain

questions.question: How many copies of a copyrighted work may a public library or archive keep for preservation?
questions.expected_answer: Up to three copies, and each copy must include a copyright notice.
questions.evidence_quote: These libraries and archives can keep up to three copies of a copyrighted work, but a copyright notice must be included on each copy.

questions.question: Under the classroom photocopying guidelines, what is the brevity limit for copying a prose work?
questions.expected_answer: No more than 2,500 words of a prose work, or 10 percent or 1,000 words of an excerpt of a prose work (and 250 words of a poem).
questions.evidence_quote: no more than 250 words of a poem, 2,500 words of a prose work, or 10 percent or 1,000 words of an excerpt of a prose work may be used

questions.question: What change did the Sonny Bono Copyright Term Extension Act make?
questions.expected_answer: It added 20 years to the copyright term, extending it for most works to the life of the author plus 70 years.
questions.evidence_quote: which added an additional 20 years to the term of copyright

questions.question: How often does the Lanham Act require trademarks to be renewed?
questions.expected_answer: Every ten years (the "deadwood" provision that clears marks no longer in commercial use).
questions.evidence_quote: required the renewal of trademarks every ten years

questions.question: Is this kind of intellectual property protection limited in duration, or can it last forever?
questions.expected_answer: Trademarks are not limited in duration; they are granted in perpetuity as long as the owner does not abandon them.
questions.evidence_quote: so they are granted in perpetuity so long as they are not abandoned by the

questions.gold_section: 5.6 Remedies Available for the Misappropriation of Trade Secrets
questions.question: How are monetary damages measured when this right is violated?
questions.filter_context: User is studying Chapter 5 (Trade Secret Basics).
questions.expected_answer: By the actual loss caused by the misappropriation plus any resulting unjust enrichment of the misappropriator; a reasonable royalty may be used if these cannot be calculated.
questions.evidence_quote: damages are measured by the actual loss caused by the misappropriation as well as any resulting unjust enrichment of the misappropriator

questions.question: Can the protected work be used freely for the purpose of parody?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, parody is one of the purposes for which copyrighted work may at times be freely used; the more transformative the new work, the less likely it infringes.
questions.evidence_quote: One of the purposes for which copyrighted work may at times be freely used is parody.

questions.question: What are the two forms of fair use?
questions.expected_answer: Nominative fair use and classic fair use.
questions.evidence_quote: These are known as nominative fair use and classic fair use.

questions.question: Which category of mark is considered the strongest?
questions.expected_answer: Fanciful marks (invented words such as Xerox, Google, Kodak); they are prima facie registrable.
questions.evidence_quote: Fanciful marks are considered the strongest type of mark and are prima facie registrable with the USPTO.

questions.question: Can a descriptive word like "Lightweight" ever be registered as a trademark?
questions.expected_answer: Not normally, but it can become eligible if it acquires a secondary meaning in the public mind through usage (e.g. "Sharp" televisions, "Windows").
questions.evidence_quote: not eligible for trademark registration unless a secondary meaning or association has been developed in the public’s mind through usage

questions.question: What two criteria must information meet to qualify as a trade secret?
questions.expected_answer: Its value must come from not being generally known, and the owner must take reasonable efforts to maintain its secrecy.
questions.evidence_quote: the information must attain its value from the fact that it is not generally known. Second, the owner of that information must take reasonable efforts to maintain its secrecy

questions.gold_section: 5.2 The Foundations of Trade Secrets Law
questions.question: When was the federal Defend Trade Secrets Act signed into law?
questions.evidence_quote: on May 11, 2016, the federal Defend Trade Secrets Act (DTSA) was signed into law

questions.question: Can a company register a mark that another business already used before it?
questions.expected_answer: Generally no (prior use bar); the only exception is when the mark was used in an entirely different market or field of business, e.g. "Progressive".
questions.evidence_quote: The only exception to the prior use bar is when the mark has been used in an entirely different market or field of business

questions.question: Within how many years must the owner bring a lawsuit, and can filing within that period still be too late?
questions.filter_context: User is studying Chapter 5 (Trade Secret Basics).
questions.expected_answer: The UTSA statute of limitations is three years, but courts can still deny relief if the action was not initiated reasonably promptly.
questions.evidence_quote: Although the statute of limitations under the UTSA is three years, courts have the power to deny the relief requested

questions.question: Can the monetary damages for infringement be increased, and if so when?
questions.expected_answer: Yes. Trademark damages compensate lost profits and may be trebled if the infringement is deemed intentional.
questions.evidence_quote: may be trebled if the infringement is deemed intentional

questions.question: If I have not used my mark in commerce yet, can I still apply to register it, and by when must I start using it?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, with an intent-to-use application based on a bona fide intent; the mark must then be put into use within six months of receiving a notice of allowance, or the applicant risks extension fees or losing the mark.
questions.evidence_quote: The mark must then be put into use within six months of receiving a “notice of allowance” from the USPTO

questions.question: After how long can a registered mark become immune from most challenges to its validity?
questions.expected_answer: If it is still in commercial use five years after registration it can gain incontestability (via a §15 Declaration), though it can still be challenged for genericism, functionality or abandonment.
questions.evidence_quote: If the trademark is still in commercial use five years after registration, the owner is eligible to receive an additional protection known as “incontestability,”

questions.question: What must a copyright holder now prove to obtain an injunction against an infringer?
questions.expected_answer: A likelihood of irreparable harm; after the 2011 Ninth Circuit ruling there is no longer a presumption of irreparable harm.
questions.evidence_quote: the plaintiff must demonstrate a likelihood of irreparable harm as a prerequisite for injunctive relief

questions.question: When an employee who knows trade secrets leaves to join another company, what factors do courts consider?
questions.expected_answer: Whether the former and new employers are competitors, whether the new position is comparable to the former one, and how effective the new employer's steps to prevent misappropriation are.
questions.evidence_quote: courts typically consider three factors: (1) whether the former employer and the new employer are competitors, (2) whether the employee’s new position is comparable to the former position, and (3) the efficacy of steps taken by the new employer to prevent the misappropriation of trade secrets
